rules.title: Annual Residential Rent Increase Limit
rules.requirement: [Basis: official explanatory text, not operative legal text] Annual residential rent increases are capped at the lower of 3% per year or 80% of the change in the Consumer Price Index over the most recent 12-month period. No rent increase is permitted if the CPI is negative.
rules.key_value: lower of 3% per year or 80% of CPI
rules.quoted_span: Increase in residential rents are limited to the lower of 3% per year, or 80% of the percent change in the Consumer Price Index over the most recent 12-month period. If the CPI is negative, no rent increase is permitted.

rules.title: Fair Return Petition for Relief from Rent Cap
rules.requirement: [Basis: official explanatory text, not operative legal text] An owner of residential rental property or a mobile home park may petition for relief from the rent cap by providing evidence that an increase above the annual allowance is necessary for a fair and reasonable return, to be decided by the City Manager or designee within 60 days of a complete application.
rules.quoted_span: Any owner of residential rental property or a mobile home park may petition for relief from the cap, but will need to provide evidence that a rate increase in excess of the annual allowance is necessary to provide a fair and reasonable return for their property. The City Manager, or designee, may consider a variety of relevant factors and will decide on the petition within 60 days of receiving a complete application.

rules.title: Written Notice of Rent Stabilization Ordinance
rules.requirement: [Basis: official explanatory text, not operative legal text] Property owners must give tenants written notice of the Rent Stabilization Ordinance and tenant rights at the start of a lease or as part of any rent increase notice.
rules.quoted_span: Property owners are required to provide written notice of the Ordinance and tenant’s rights at commencement of a lease or as part of any notice to increase rent.

rules.title: Just Cause Requirement for Tenancy Termination
rules.requirement: [Basis: official explanatory text, not operative legal text] After 30 days of tenancy, a property owner may not terminate a tenancy without just cause, which must be stated in a written notice.
rules.quoted_span: After 30 days, an owner shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause, which shall be stated in a written notice.

rules.title: At-Fault Just Cause Grounds
rules.requirement: [Basis: official explanatory text, not operative legal text] Allowable at-fault grounds for termination of tenancy include default in payment of rent, breach of a material lease term, committing a nuisance, criminal activity, and other specified actions.
rules.quoted_span: “Just cause” includes certain at-fault causes such as default in payment of rent, breach of a material term of the lease, committing a nuisance, criminal activity, and other actions.

rules.title: No-Fault Just Cause Grounds
rules.requirement: [Basis: official explanatory text, not operative legal text] Allowable no-fault grounds for termination of tenancy include owner intent to occupy the property, withdrawal of the property from the rental market, and demolition or substantial remodel.
rules.quoted_span: “Just cause” also includes certain no-fault causes such as the intent of the owner to occupy the property, removal of the property from the rental market, and demolition or substantial remodel.

rules.title: Notice and Opportunity to Cure Violation
rules.requirement: [Basis: official explanatory text, not operative legal text] An owner must provide notice of the violation and give the tenant a time period to fix the violation before issuing a notice to terminate tenancy for just cause.
rules.quoted_span: Before issuing a notice to terminate for just cause, the owner shall first give notice of the violation with a time period for the tenant to fix the violation(s).

rules.title: Relocation Assistance or Rent Waiver for No-Fault Terminations
rules.requirement: [Basis: official explanatory text, not operative legal text] For a no-fault just cause termination, the owner must either provide 3 months of relocation assistance or waive rent for the last 3 months of the tenancy.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies under a no-fault just cause termination.
rules.quoted_span: Under a no-fault just cause termination, the owner shall either provide 3 months of relocation assistance or waive payment of rent for the final 3 months of the tenancy.

rules.title: Tenant Notice of Just Cause Eviction Protections
rules.requirement: [Basis: official explanatory text, not operative legal text] Property owners must provide notice of Just Cause Eviction Ordinance protections to existing tenants before December 19, 2021, or upon the commencement or renewal of a lease.
rules.quoted_span: Property owners must provide notice to existing tenants before December 19, 2021, or at commencement or renewal of their lease of the Just Cause Eviction Ordinance protections.

provisions.summary: Limits residential rent increases to the lower of 3% per year or 80% of CPI change, and prohibits increases if CPI is negative.
Permits property owners to petition for fair return relief from the annual rent increase cap.
Requires owners to provide written notice of the ordinance and tenant rights at lease commencement or with rent increase notices.
Prohibits terminating tenancies after 30 days without just cause stated in a written notice.
Enumerates permitted at-fault grounds for termination of tenancy.
Enumerates permitted no-fault grounds for termination of tenancy.
Requires notice of violation and opportunity to cure before issuing a notice to terminate for just cause.
Requires 3 months relocation assistance or waiver of the final 3 months rent for no-fault terminations.
Requires notice of Just Cause Eviction Ordinance protections to existing tenants before December 19, 2021, or at lease commencement/renewal.
